title: Depravity and mysteries above nature both demand the Spirit's work for faith
pass_a_gloss: Further, the perversity of the human mind, and the darkness that sin has brought on, make that operation of God's Spirit in our souls necessary. For sacred Scripture contains many things that clash with our depraved and twisted affections. Hence the carnal man shrinks from it and turns away, which keeps him from acknowledging its truth and forming a right judgment about it: for each person judges according as he is affected. Next, the human mind as a whole is so darkened by sin that even in natural things it cannot help hallucinating and is very often deceived. And therefore much less can it certainly acknowledge and perceive things that are above nature. For this, then, it is necessary that the Holy Spirit dispel the mind's native darkness and those fumes by which wicked affections darken the intellect and hinder it from discerning the truth. Indeed, not only our nature's depravity and the darkness sprung from sin, but the very genius of the doctrine handed down in Scripture, necessarily demands this Spirit operation for generating faith in our souls. For it contains many mysteries that altogether surpass not only corrupt nature but human nature considered in itself, even apart from sin: so that by that nature they can not only not be invented and thought out, but cannot even be understood and perceived. And therefore it is necessary that the Holy Spirit not only heal our minds blinded by sin, but also raise our intellect not a little above its natural state, so that it can rise to such great things.
pass_b_english: Human crookedness, plus the darkness sin has piled on, forces this need for God's Spirit in the soul. Scripture is full of matter that fights our warped loves. The flesh-bound person therefore recoils and turns away — and that recoil blocks true acknowledgment and right judgment, because we all judge by the grain of our affections.

Sin also darkens the mind so thoroughly that even among ordinary natural things we keep hallucinating and falling into error. How much less, then, can we be sure of what stands above nature? So the Holy Spirit must drive out the mind's native night, and clear the smoke by which wicked desires cloud the intellect and stop it from seeing truth.

Nor is depravity the only reason. The very character of the doctrine Scripture teaches also requires this Spirit work if faith is to be born in us. Scripture holds mysteries that outrun not only fallen nature but human nature taken by itself, even without sin. Nature cannot invent them, think them up, or even understand and take them in. So the Spirit must heal minds sin has blinded, and must also lift the intellect well above its natural level, until it can rise to things that great.
source_text:
IV. Porro istam Spiritus Dei in animis nostris operationem necessariam reddit ingenii humani pravitas, et tenebrae quas peccatum accersivit. Etenim Scriptura sacra multa continet, quae pravis et distortis nostris affectibus repugnant. Unde fit ut homo carnalis ab illa abhorreat, et eam aversetur, quod impedit ne ejus veritatem agnoscat, et rectum de ea judicium ferat: quandoquidem prout quisque affectus est, ita judicat. Deinde mens hominis in universum ita per peccatum obscurata est, ut, etiam in naturalibus, non possit non hallucinari, et saepissime falli. Ac proinde multo minus quae supra naturam sunt certo agnoscere et percipere potest. Ad hoc igitur necesse est, ut Spiritus sanctus mentis tenebras nativas dispellat, et fumos illos, quibus affectus pravi intellectum obscurant, et praepediunt ne possit veritatem cernere.

V. Imo hanc Spiritus operationem ad fidem animis nostris ingenerandam necessario exigit, non tantum naturae nostrae depravatio, et tenebrae ex peccato ortae, sed genius ipse doctrinae in Scriptura traditae. Siquidem multa mysteria continet, quae non tantum naturam corruptam, sed naturam humanam in se, etiam citra peccatum, consideratam, omnino superant: ita ut ab ea, non solum non inveniri et excogitari, sed nec intelligi et percipi possint. Ideoque necesse est, ut Spiritus sanctus non tantum mentes nostras peccato caecas sanet, sed etiam ut intellectum nostrum non parum supra statum naturalem extollat, ut ad res tantas possit assurgere.
